title: “मार्यो च्याङ्बा मार्यो असिनामा पारयो” कथाको सबाल्टर्न विश्लेषण "Maryo Chyangba Maryo Asinama Paryo" Kathako Sabaltern Vishleshan
authors: कोइराला Koirala, नरेन्द्र Narendra प्रसाद Prasad
nepali: प्रस्तुत लेखमा कथाकार मनु ब्राजाकीद्वारा लिखित मा¥यो च्याङ्बा मा¥यो असिनामा पा¥यो कथालार्ई सबाल्टर्न सिद्धान्तका कोणबाट विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । सदियौँदेखि इतिहास विहीन भएका वा बनाइएका समाजका किनारामा रहेका आवाज विहीन तथा अधिकार विहीन समूदाय नै सबाल्टर्न वर्ग हुन् । सबाल्टर्न एउटा बृहत् सिद्धान्त हो । यसभित्र सबै प्रकारका विभेदहरूका कारण किनारीकृत हुन पुगेका सबै शोषित पीडितहरू अटाउन सक्ने भए पनि यस लेखमा प्रस्तुत कथामा सबाल्टर्न वर्गको वर्गीय, लैङ्गिक र जातीय अवस्था पहिचान गरी समाजमा (कथामा) उनीहरूकोे स्थान, उनीहरूमाथिको प्रभुत्व र उनीहरूको प्रतिरोधको अवस्थाको विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । यस कथामा वर्गीय दृष्टिले निम्न वर्ग, जातीय दृष्टिले निम्न जात (अछुत) र लैङ्गिक दृष्टिले नारी सबाल्टर्न पात्रका रूपमा देखिएका छन् भने उनीहरूको प्रतिनिधित्व समाजसापेक्ष छ, उच्च वर्गीय प्रभुत्वको चक्रमा पिसिएकै कारण उनीहरू सबाल्टर्न हुन पुगेका भए पनि उनीहरूमा प्रतिरोध चेतना न्यून रहेको छ भन्ने निष्कर्ष निकालिएको छ ।
american_english: In this article, the story "Maryo Chyangba Maryo Asinama Paryo" written by storyteller Manu Brajaki is analyzed from the perspective of subaltern theory. The subaltern class consists of voiceless and rightless communities on the margins of societies that have been without history, or have had history made for them, for centuries. Subaltern is a vast theory. Although all oppressed and suffering people who have been pushed to the margins because of all kinds of discrimination can be encompassed within it, in this article the story presented identifies the class, gender, and caste conditions of the subaltern class and analyzes their place in society (in the story), the dominance exercised over them, and the state of their resistance. In this story, the lower class from a class perspective, the lower caste (untouchable) from a caste perspective, and women from a gender perspective are seen as subaltern characters, and while their representation is relative to society, the conclusion is drawn that although they became subaltern because they were crushed in the cycle of upper-class dominance, the consciousness of resistance among them remains low.

informal_english: In this article, the story "Maryo Chyangba Maryo Asinama Paryo" written by storyteller Manu Brajaki is looked at from the angle of subaltern theory. Sure, the subaltern class is made up of voiceless and rightless communities stuck on the margins of societies that have been without history, or have had history made for them, for centuries. Subaltern is a massive theory altogether. Even though all the oppressed and suffering people who've been shoved to the margins because of all sorts of discrimination can be taken in by it, in this article the story at hand picks out the class, gender, and caste conditions of the subaltern class and looks at their place in society (in the story), the dominance they're under, and where they stand with resistance. In this story, the lower class from a class point of view, the lower caste (untouchable) from a caste point of view, and women from a gender point of view come across as subaltern characters, and while how they're represented is tied to society, the conclusion is that even though they ended up subaltern because they were ground down in the cycle of upper-class dominance, the sense of resistance in them is still fairly low.
